A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same WIR3D work. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison despite rearrangements.

before.justification: v1 reports original shape-abstraction experiments, baseline comparisons, ablations, application demonstrations, and a 96-person perceptual study.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds photo-reconstruction examples and a separate 42-person deformation preference study.

M1.justification: The two-stage procedure and principal loss components persist. Section 3.3 changes the stage-II backbone from RN50x16 to RN50x64, but Appendix G still specifies RN50x16. Equation (6) also changes its formulation; the PDFs do not clearly establish whether these differences reflect procedural changes or corrections to the description.

E1.justification: v2 adds evaluation on defective photo-reconstructed meshes from Real-World-Textured Things: a shoe and a sculpture in Figure 7. This extends input-condition coverage, while the existing datasets, object and scene abstraction, refinement, and deformation tasks remain.

E2.justification: ARAP is newly evaluated against WIR3D for deformation in Section 4.4. NEF and 3Doodle remain the abstraction comparators, with unchanged membership in Table 1.

E3.justification: v2 adds a separate 42-person deformation preference protocol comparing a dragged WIR3D control point with the nearest ARAP vertex. Appendix E changes refinement from 300 to 100 iterations. Section 3.3 also reports a backbone-size revision contradicted by Appendix G; none of these disclosures establishes that the retained benchmark experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Figure 7 adds a robustness demonstration on meshes with boundary and non-manifold defects. The random-keypoint comparison changes from the dragon in v1 Figure 18 to Nefertiti in v2 Figure 9, alongside meaningful-keypoint and no-keypoint conditions. The principal ablations and Table 2 remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new study reports a preference percentage using the existing reporting practice; its participant count changes evaluation design rather than uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 1 and 2 retain every numerical result, including the 88% preference over 3Doodle. v2 separately reports 80% preference over ARAP among 42 respondents, adds photo-reconstruction outcomes, and replaces the illustrated random-keypoint result. The two preference percentages concern different studies, not a performance decline.

T1.justification: Equation (6) replaces the coordinate-indexed projection expression P(B_i)_j with a sum over projected curve positions P(B_i(t)), revising the formal view-regularization definition. The other loss equations and camera-projection assumption remain; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the same contributions: sparse geometry- and texture-aware 3D curves, localized keypoint supervision, surface adherence, and refinement/deformation applications. The added experiments support these existing claims.

C2.justification: v2 attributes robustness to defective geometry to CLIP's global semantic understanding and interprets the ARAP comparison as evidence of better semantic preservation during deformation. The keypoint-quality and preprocessing-time limitations remain, although their discussion is shortened.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies 20 curves per stage and a matched 40-curve budget for 3Doodle, while noting that NEF cannot control curve count. The revised refinement budget and conflicting backbone specifications also change reproducibility information. Both versions still promise a future code release.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for Real-World Textured Things and As-Rigid-As-Possible Surface Modeling, supporting the new examples and comparison. The existing related-work discussion and principal novelty positioning are otherwise retained.

P1.justification: v2 tightens introductory and experimental prose, consolidates ablation discussion, moves multi-view fidelity discussion to Appendix F, shortens limitations, and adds acknowledgements. These are localized edits within the retained document structure.

P2.justification: v2 adds the reconstruction figure, deformation comparison inset, and deformation-study screenshots. It reworks keypoint comparisons into main-text Figure 9, trims some existing panels, and rearranges figures and tables. Most diagrams, result galleries, and both table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: The reconstruction examples and ARAP preference study provide useful additional support for robustness and deformation utility, which v1 supported mainly through demonstrations. Explicit curve budgets also improve comparison transparency. These limited gains are partly offset by the new RN50x64/RN50x16 inconsistency between Section 3.3 and Appendix G; the primary quantitative evidence remains unchanged.
